pr.body: Create recovery keys in user storage or local. Closes https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/38445
pr.title: Create recovery keys in user storage or local

raw_findings.body: The credential model built via createFromValues() never receives the ID that updateCredential() carefully stored via setId(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()) (R195), so consumers see a credential with a null ID; removal by ID becomes removeStoredCredentialById(null) and credential listings/deletions keyed by ID fail, whereas the OTP path was explicitly fixed in this same patch (R179) to always carry an ID
raw_findings.failure_mode: Federated recovery-codes credential is exposed with a null ID, breaking ID-based operations such as removal after code exhaustion and credential listing
raw_findings.impact: The credential model built via createFromValues() never receives the ID that updateCredential() carefully stored via setId(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()) (R195), so consumers see a credential with a null ID; removal by ID becomes removeStoredCredentialById(null) and credential listings/deletions keyed by ID fail, whereas the OTP path was explicitly fixed in this same patch (R179) to always carry an ID
raw_findings.root_cause: getCredentials() reconstructs the recovery-codes credential with RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(), which never sets an ID, and the stored model's generated ID is not propagated
raw_findings.suggested_fix: After building the model in getCredentials(), copy the identifier from the stored record, e.g. model.setId(myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()), mirroring what the OTP branch now guarantees
raw_findings.title: Federated recovery-codes credential returned by getCredentials has no ID, unlike the stored model and the OTP counterpart
raw_findings.trigger: Any caller that consumes user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream() for a federated user with recovery codes, e.g. RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator calling removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()) after all codes are used, or account/admin endpoints listing credentials by ID

raw_findings.body: NullPointerException is thrown from getCredentials(), aborting credential enumeration for the user instead of returning an empty stream, unlike isConfiguredFor()/getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() which explicitly null-check getMyUser(user)
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled NPE during federated credential enumeration for a user missing from the provider's map
raw_findings.impact: NullPointerException is thrown from getCredentials(), aborting credential enumeration for the user instead of returning an empty stream, unlike isConfiguredFor()/getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() which explicitly null-check getMyUser(user)
raw_findings.root_cause: New getCredentials() override omits the myUser == null guard that all other overrides in this class apply after getMyUser()
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a null check at the top of getCredentials(): if (myUser == null) return Stream.empty();
raw_findings.title: getCredentials() dereferences getMyUser(user) without the null guard used by every sibling method
raw_findings.trigger: getFederatedCredentialsStream() is invoked for a UserModel whose federation link points to this provider but whose username is no longer present in the in-memory users map (e.g. a cached UserModel after the entry was removed, or username translation mismatch)

raw_findings.body: In this compat storage a recovery code is infinitely reusable and out-of-order codes are accepted, diverging from RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider semantics (removeRecoveryAuthnCode + updateStoredCredential); the new testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin therefore cannot catch regressions in code consumption or next-code selection for federated users
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test provider's validation semantics are weaker than production semantics, masking reuse/ordering defects in the federated recovery-codes flow
raw_findings.impact: In this compat storage a recovery code is infinitely reusable and out-of-order codes are accepted, diverging from RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider semantics (removeRecoveryAuthnCode + updateStoredCredential); the new testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin therefore cannot catch regressions in code consumption or next-code selection for federated users
raw_findings.root_cause: isValid() implements recovery-code checking as an unordered anyMatch over the raw code list without mutating stored state
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Validate only the head code of the stored list (matching the displayed next-code number), remove it from the persisted list on success, and extend the test to assert a used code is rejected on a second login
raw_findings.title: Federated recovery-code validation accepts any stored code and never consumes it, so one-time-use and code-ordering regressions cannot be detected
raw_findings.trigger: A federated user authenticates with recovery codes: the login page (driven by getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()) always shows code #1 because the stored list is never updated, yet isValid() matches any of the 12 codes and never removes the used one

raw_findings.body: removeStoredCredentialById() targets the Keycloak-local/federated attribute store, not the user-storage provider that produced the credential, and the federated model's ID may be null (as in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials); the exhausted credential is never removed from the storage provider, so it keeps being surfaced and the removal call silently fails or throws
raw_findings.failure_mode: Exhausted federated recovery-codes credential cannot be deleted, leaving stale state and a possible exception during login
raw_findings.impact: removeStoredCredentialById() targets the Keycloak-local/federated attribute store, not the user-storage provider that produced the credential, and the federated model's ID may be null (as in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials); the exhausted credential is never removed from the storage provider, so it keeps being surfaced and the removal call silently fails or throws
raw_findings.root_cause: R80 widens the credential lookup to federated credentials but the downstream cleanup path still assumes the credential lives in local storage
raw_findings.suggested_fix: When the credential originates from getFederatedCredentialsStream(), skip removeStoredCredentialById() (or delegate removal to the storage provider via disableCredentialType/updateCredential) instead of assuming a locally stored credential
raw_findings.title: getCredential() may return a federated credential that the authenticator then tries to remove from local storage by ID
raw_findings.trigger: A federated user whose user-storage provider returns a recovery-codes credential from getCredentials() with all codes used (allCodesUsed() true); the subsequent unchanged code calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())

raw_findings.body: The alias contains a typo ("suthenticator" instead of "authenticator"), reducing searchability and consistency with the delayed-authenticator provider ID it configures
raw_findings.failure_mode: Maintainability defect: inconsistent, misspelled configuration identifier in test code

raw_findings.trigger: Anyone reading or searching flow configuration aliases while debugging this test (e.g. grepping for "delayed-authenticator-config")

raw_findings.body: disableCredentialType() falls into its else branch and logs "Unsupported to disable credential", so the recovery-codes credential silently remains in the storage and can never be disabled/removed through the manager, and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() never advertises it
raw_findings.failure_mode: Disable/remove operations for federated recovery codes silently no-op, leaving the credential active
raw_findings.impact: disableCredentialType() falls into its else branch and logs "Unsupported to disable credential", so the recovery-codes credential silently remains in the storage and can never be disabled/removed through the manager, and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() never advertises it
raw_findings.root_cause: supportsCredentialType() was broadened to the recovery-codes type without updating the disable/removal code paths in the same class
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Extend disableCredentialType() to clear myUser.recoveryCodes and add RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE to getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() when the user has recovery codes
raw_findings.title: supportsCredentialType() now claims recovery-codes support while disableCredentialType() and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() do not handle it
raw_findings.trigger: UserCredentialManager.disableCredentialType() is invoked for a federated user with credentialType "recovery-authn-codes" (e.g. account/admin credential removal): the manager checks updater.supportsCredentialType() which now returns true and delegates to disableCredentialType()

validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch R135 verbatim shows config.setAlias("delayed-suthenticator-config") which is a typo of 'authenticator'. This is a stylistic/maintainability issue but the typo is clearly introduced by the patch.

validated_findings.body: disableCredentialType() falls into its else branch and logs "Unsupported to disable credential", so the recovery-codes credential silently remains in the storage and can never be disabled/removed through the manager, and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() never advertises it
validated_findings.failure_mode: Disable/remove operations for federated recovery codes silently no-op, leaving the credential active
validated_findings.impact: disableCredentialType() falls into its else branch and logs "Unsupported to disable credential", so the recovery-codes credential silently remains in the storage and can never be disabled/removed through the manager, and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() never advertises it
validated_findings.root_cause: supportsCredentialType() was broadened to the recovery-codes type without updating the disable/removal code paths in the same class
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Extend disableCredentialType() to clear myUser.recoveryCodes and add RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE to getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() when the user has recovery codes
validated_findings.title: supportsCredentialType() now claims recovery-codes support while disableCredentialType() and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() do not handle it
validated_findings.trigger: UserCredentialManager.disableCredentialType() is invoked for a federated user with credentialType "recovery-authn-codes" (e.g. account/admin credential removal): the manager checks updater.supportsCredentialType() which now returns true and delegates to disableCredentialType()
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch R114 adds RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE to supportsCredentialType(), but disableCredentialType() at R217-223 only handles isOTPType and logs 'Unsupported' for other types. getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() at R254 also doesn't include recovery codes. This inconsistency is introduced by the patch.
